text:
maria_customer: Hey team, since yesterday our dedicated pool started returning a lot of 429s and slow tails. Spike around 18:20 UTC. App logs show long context requests (token_count ~ 45k) and frequent retries. Can someone look?

rachel: Sorry about that—can you paste a sample request id and approximate timestamps? 429 rate % and any error body would help.

maria_customer: Request IDs: req-8f7a2 and req-8f7a9 around 2025-12-04T18:19:34Z. 429 body: `\{"error\":\"request throttled: kv_cache_eviction\"}`. Overall 5% request_failures and p95 latency 2.4s -> 6.3s.

rachel: Thanks. This sounds like KV cache pressure from long-context tenants. Assigning infra. @devin can you pull eviction counters for that dedicated pool (pool-id: ded-ord-12)?

devin: Pulling now. Quick snapshot shows eviction_rate spiked to 11k/s at 18:19 UTC, resident_kv_shards showing heavy fragmentation, and freeable_memory dropping under reservation threshold. Suspect long-context workloads are forcing frequent prefix evictions which degrade throughput + cause internal throttles.

rachel: Did autoscaler kick? Customer says they are on reserved capacity and didn't expect autoscale to drop them.

devin: Autoscaler didn't scale down; we hit internal backpressure path that starts rejecting when kv_eviction_backlog > 5k. That's a safety throttle to protect host OOM. Backpressure rule: if eviction_queue_length > 5000 and kernel page reclaim > 0.8 -> throttle 10-50% depending on severity.

maria_customer: Is there a short mitigation we can do on our side? We can't change model usage right now quickly.

rachel: Short-term options: 1) reduce max_context_length for high-traffic routes (truncate earlier), 2) enable per-tenant aggressive prefix caching (helps if many requests share prefixes), 3) request a temporary capacity bump (dedicated burst or add another pool). We can also apply an emergency eviction_tuning patch on infra side to make eviction less CPU-heavy.

devin: To debug further, can you run a quick repro script to capture a failing request with KV metrics? Example curl:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"open-llama-70b", "input":"<long chat...>", "max_tokens":512, "client_request_id":"req-REPRO-1"}'
```

and then capture: `/var/log/redwood/runtime/kv-stats.log` around the timestamp and `journalctl -u redwood-runtime --since "2025-12-04 18:18:00" --until "2025-12-04 18:22:00"`.

maria_customer: Running now, sending req-REPRO-1. Will paste logs.

maria_customer: Paste: `kv_evictions: 11245/s, eviction_queue: 8620, kv_frag_ratio: 0.42, kv_bytes_in_use: 78GB, kv_heap_free: 1.2GB`

devin: That matches. kv_heap_free low and fragmentation high. Kernel logs show lots of page faults at same window. This screams memory fragmentation + long-lived KV slabs preventing efficient compaction.

oliver: We recently rolled a runtime patch that changed small-slab allocation thresholds (rolling out last week). Could be interacting with long contexts. I'll check rollout notes.

oliver: Confirmed: rollout id r2025-11-29-9 adjusted slab_size_cutover. Some pods in ded-ord-12 still on old binary, some on new -> mixed allocation behavior could increase fragmentation.

rachel: Mixed binaries on same pool is bad for KV locality. Can infra schedule a controlled drain and ensure homogeneous binary?

devin: We can abort the partial rollout and force a homogeneous restart of pool ded-ord-12. Plan: cordon pool, drain 25% at a time, restart with binary r2025-11-30-13 which contains a fragmentation mitigation. Expected ~6-8 min per batch. Will set maintenance window now if you approve.

maria_customer: Please do. Our traffic is already impacted. We'll enable client-side short-term truncation for heavy routes (apply in 5 min).

rachel: Approving. @devin proceed and keep me posted. Also enable temporary rate limit override for this tenant to avoid cascading retries (set to 60% of usual).

devin: Starting drain now. rolling restarts + eviction-tuning enabled. Watching kv_evictions...

sre-bot: [automated] pool ded-ord-12 maintenance started by devin at 2025-12-04T18:30:12Z. Estimated duration 20m.

devin: 18:36 update: eviction_rate down to 3.2k/s, eviction_queue 900, kv_frag_ratio now 0.27, p95 latency improved to 1.1s. 429s dropping.

maria_customer: Seeing improvement on our side, thanks. Can you share suggested long-term fixes?

rachel: Long-term: 1) Avoid mixed binary rollouts across same dedicated pool; use pool-wide canary. 2) Expose per-tenant KV reservations so noisy tenants can't fragment pool memory. 3) Improve allocation compaction and opportunistic defrag in runtime. 4) Add observability: per-tenant KV fragmentation and hot-shard alerts. 5) Offer model/sequence length quotas as opt-in for Dedicated customers.

devin: Also include autoscaler policy change: when eviction_queue > threshold, autoscaler should proactively add capacity (if available) rather than only applying local backpressure. We'll open a ticket.

oliver: I'm filing a follow-up to revert mixed rollout controls and add a preflight check that pool has homogeneous runtime version.

rachel: Great. maria_customer, we'll follow up in this thread with the maintenance closure and postmortem. For now leaving emergency rate-limit override and eviction-tuning for 1 hour. :thumbsup:

maria_customer: Thank you all — performance looks stable. Appreciate the quick response.

sre-bot: [automated] pool ded-ord-12 maintenance completed at 2025-12-04T18:48:07Z.

rachel: Closing loop — creating internal follow-up: JIRA INF-7892 (KV fragmentation root cause + rollout hardening). Will share postmortem once done.
